name: Helly's theorem
description: If a finite family of at least d+1 convex sets in R^d has the property that every d+1 of them have a common point, then the whole family has a common point.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Radon's theorem
description: Any set of d+2 points in R^d can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets whose convex hulls have a common point (a Radon partition).
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Caratheodory's theorem
description: If a point x lies in the convex hull of a set S in R^d, then x lies in the convex hull of some subset of S of at most d+1 points.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Tverberg's theorem
description: Any set of (r-1)(d+1)+1 points in R^d can be partitioned into r parts whose convex hulls have a common point (a Tverberg partition).
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Colorful Caratheodory theorem
description: Given d+1 sets (color classes) in R^d each whose convex hull contains a point x, there is a rainbow selection of one point from each class whose convex hull contains x (Barany 1982).
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Colorful Helly theorem
description: Given d+1 finite color classes of convex sets in R^d such that every rainbow transversal (one set per class) has a common point, then some single color class has a common point (Lovasz, via Barany 1982).
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Fractional Helly theorem
description: For convex sets in R^d, if an alpha-fraction of the (d+1)-tuples have a common point, then some beta(alpha,d)n of the sets have a common point, with the sharp bound beta = 1-(1-alpha)^{1/(d+1)} (Katchalski-Liu 1979; sharp form Kalai 1984, Eckhoff).
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: (p,q)-theorem (Hadwiger-Debrunner / Alon-Kleitman)
description: For p >= q > d, any finite family of convex sets in R^d with the (p,q)-property (among every p sets some q have a common point) can be pierced by a bounded number f(p,q,d) of points.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Topological Helly theorem
description: For a good cover (a family of open sets in R^d all of whose nonempty intersections are contractible), if every d+1 sets intersect then all sets have a common point.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Upper bound theorem for convex sets
description: Bounds the number of k-fold intersection points of n convex sets in R^d in which no d+r+1 sets have a common point, in terms of the number of empty intersections (Kalai 1984, Eckhoff 1985).
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Topological Tverberg conjecture
description: Conjecture that for any continuous map from the (d+1)(r-1)-simplex to R^d there exist r pairwise vertex-disjoint faces whose images have a common point; true for r a prime power and disproved by Frick for general r.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Sierksma's conjecture
description: Conjecture that the number of Tverberg r-partitions of any (r-1)(d+1)+1 points in general position in R^d is at least ((r-1)!)^d.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Cascade conjecture
description: Kalai's conjecture that if the sum over i of (1+dim T_i(A)) for i=1..r-1 is less than |A| then the r-fold Tverberg set T_r(A) is nonempty, interpolating between Radon and Tverberg.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Nerve complex method
description: Encoding the intersection pattern of a family of sets as a simplicial complex (the nerve) whose combinatorial-topological properties such as d-collapsibility or being d-Leray drive Helly-type bounds.
source_article: Helly-type problems, Imre Barany and Gil Kalai, 2022

name: Nisan-Wigderson pseudorandom generator
description: An explicit construction of a pseudorandom generator from a function hard for small circuits, using a combinatorial design of nearly disjoint index sets to fool bounded-size circuits.
source_article: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Impagliazzo-Wigderson theorem (hardness vs randomness)
description: If some problem in E (deterministic exponential time) requires Boolean circuits of size 2^{Omega(n)}, then P = BPP, i.e. randomized polynomial time can be fully derandomized.
source_article: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Hardness amplification (Yao XOR lemma / direct product)
description: Method that converts a function mildly hard on average into one extremely hard on average by taking XORs or direct products of independent instances.
source_article: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Zig-zag product of graphs
description: A graph product (Reingold-Vadhan-Wigderson) combining a large graph with a small one to produce expanders of controlled degree, yielding an iterative combinatorial construction of expander families.
source_article: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: SL = L theorem (Reingold)
description: Undirected s-t connectivity can be decided in deterministic logarithmic space, equivalently symmetric logspace equals logspace, proved via the zig-zag product.
source_article: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Operator scaling / noncommutative optimization
description: A geodesically-convex alternating-minimization algorithm over symmetric (group-orbit) spaces that scales tuples of matrices toward doubly balanced form, solving null-cone and noncommutative singularity problems and instances of polynomial identity testing.
source_article: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Efficiency gap
description: A scalar measure of partisan advantage in a districting plan equal to the normalized difference between the two parties' total wasted votes (votes for losers plus surplus votes for winners).
source_article: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Jordan S. Ellenberg, 2021

name: Partisan symmetry
description: The criterion that a districting plan's seats-votes curve be invariant under swapping the two parties' roles, i.e. symmetric under (x,y) -> (1-x,1-y).
source_article: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Jordan S. Ellenberg, 2021

name: Ensemble (outlier) analysis of districting plans
description: Detecting partisan gerrymanders by generating a large random sample of legally valid districting plans and testing whether an enacted plan is a statistical outlier relative to that ensemble.
source_article: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Jordan S. Ellenberg, 2021

name: Recombination (ReCom) Markov chain
description: A Markov chain on balanced graph partitions that merges two adjacent districts, samples a uniform spanning tree of the union, and splits it along an edge into two balanced connected parts, mixing far faster than single-unit flip walks.
source_article: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Jordan S. Ellenberg, 2021

name: Chikina-Frieze-Pegden local outlier test
description: For a reversible Markov chain, a rigorous statistical significance bound on a plan being an outlier can be obtained from short random walks without knowing the mixing time, with false-positive probability at most 2 sqrt(epsilon).
source_article: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Jordan S. Ellenberg, 2021

name: NP-hardness of balanced connected graph partition
description: Sampling or counting balanced partitions of a weighted planar graph into connected pieces of equal weight is NP-hard, even into two parts, formalizing the computational difficulty of districting.
source_article: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Jordan S. Ellenberg, 2021

name: Sunflower (Delta-system)
description: A collection of r sets in which all pairwise intersections equal one common core (kernel), so that the parts outside the core (petals) are pairwise disjoint.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Erdos-Rado sunflower lemma
description: Any family of more than w!(r-1)^w sets each of size at most w contains an r-sunflower.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Sunflower conjecture
description: Conjecture of Erdos and Rado that for each r there is a constant c(r) such that any family of more than c(r)^w sets of size at most w contains an r-sunflower.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang sunflower bound
description: Any family of more than (C r log w log log w)^w sets of size at most w contains an r-sunflower, an almost-quasipolynomial-per-element improvement toward the sunflower conjecture.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Spread (robust sunflower) family
description: A weighted set family is r-spread if for every set T the total weight of members containing T is at most r^{-|T|} of the whole, a pseudorandomness condition forcing the family to look uniformly spread out.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Kahn-Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture (Park-Pham theorem)
description: For any monotone property, the threshold probability is at most a logarithmic factor times the expectation threshold (the fractional/expectation lower bound), proved by Park and Pham via spread families.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Random restriction with spreadness
description: Proof technique that repeatedly applies random restrictions to a spread set family, shrinking set sizes while preserving approximate spreadness until a sunflower is forced, with Janson-type inequalities at the base case.
source_article: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Boolean social choice function
description: A function assigning a societal outcome to a profile of voter preferences (e.g. a Boolean function aggregating n voters' binary opinions), the basic object of probabilistic social choice theory.
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Arrow's impossibility theorem
description: Any social welfare function on three or more alternatives that is unanimous and satisfies independence of irrelevant alternatives must be a dictatorship.
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Quantitative Arrow theorem
description: A robust version of Arrow's theorem stating that any aggregation rule that is epsilon-far from every dictatorship produces an irrational (non-transitive) outcome with probability bounded below polynomially in epsilon.
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem
description: Any surjective, non-dictatorial voting rule on three or more alternatives is manipulable: some voter can misreport preferences to obtain a better outcome.
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Quantitative Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem
description: Any voting rule on three or more alternatives that is epsilon-far from the family of nonmanipulable functions is manipulable for a random profile with probability at least inverse-polynomial in n, the number of alternatives, and 1/epsilon.
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Majority is Stablest theorem
description: Among low-influence Boolean functions, weighted majority maximizes noise stability, with the optimal value given by Borell's Gaussian noise-stability bound (Mossel, O'Donnell, Oleszkiewicz).
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Invariance principle for low-influence functions
description: A nonlinear central-limit-type theorem showing that a low-degree multilinear polynomial in independent low-influence variables has nearly the same distribution whether the inputs are Boolean or Gaussian, the key tool reducing discrete social choice problems to Gaussian geometry.
source_article: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022

name: Cap set
description: A subset of (Z/3Z)^n containing no three distinct points in arithmetic progression (equivalently no affine line), the extremal object of the cap set problem.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Slice rank of a tensor
description: The minimum number of terms needed to write a tensor (function of several variables) as a sum of products each of which depends in one factor on a single variable group and in the other on the rest (Tao's symmetric generalization of matrix rank).
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Croot-Lev-Pach lemma
description: A low-degree multilinear polynomial that vanishes off the diagonal of a finite-field cube has a number of nonzero diagonal entries bounded by twice the dimension of the relevant low-degree polynomial space.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Ellenberg-Gijswijt cap set theorem
description: Every cap set in (Z/3Z)^n has size at most c^n with c approximately 2.756, i.e. exponentially smaller than 3^n, resolving the cap set problem.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Slice rank polynomial method
description: Proof technique that bounds the size of combinatorial configurations by encoding them as a tensor supported on a diagonal, bounding its slice rank from below by the support size and from above via low-degree polynomials.
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Sunflower-free / tri-colored sum-free bounds via slice rank
description: Application of the slice rank method giving exponential upper bounds on sunflower-free set systems and on tri-colored sum-free sets in abelian groups (Naslund-Sawin, Blasiak et al.).
source_article: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Matroid
description: A finite set together with a rank function (or family of independent sets) abstracting the combinatorics of linear independence, satisfying hereditary and exchange axioms.
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Chow ring of a matroid
description: A graded commutative ring built from the flats of a matroid (via the Bergman fan / order complex) that plays the role of the cohomology of a smooth projective variety even for nonrealizable matroids.
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Kahler package for matroids
description: The Chow ring of any matroid satisfies Poincare duality, the hard Lefschetz theorem, and the Hodge-Riemann relations, despite the absence of an underlying variety (Adiprasito-Huh-Katz).
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Heron-Rota-Welsh conjecture (theorem)
description: The coefficients of the reduced characteristic polynomial of any matroid form a log-concave sequence, proved via the Hodge-Riemann relations on the Chow ring.
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Dowling-Wilson top-heavy theorem
description: For any matroid the number of flats of rank k is at most the number of flats of corank k for k below half the rank, i.e. the Whitney numbers of the second kind are top-heavy (Braden-Huh-Matherne-Proudfoot-Wang).
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Mason's log-concavity conjecture (theorem)
description: The numbers of independent sets of each size in a matroid form an (ultra) log-concave sequence, established via the Hodge-theoretic / Lorentzian polynomial framework (Adiprasito-Huh-Katz, Anari et al., Brandén-Huh).
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Hodge-Riemann relations (combinatorial use)
description: Establishing inequalities (log-concavity, top-heaviness) by proving that a bilinear form on a degree-graded ring is nondegenerate with prescribed signature, transferring algebraic positivity to combinatorial sequences.
source_article: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids since June Huh, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Classical verification of quantum computation
description: A protocol in which a polynomial-time classical verifier interacts with a single untrusted quantum prover and accepts only if the prover correctly performs a claimed quantum computation (the BQP verification problem).
source_article: Verifying quantum computations at scale: a cryptographic leash on quantum devices, Thomas Vidick, 2020

name: Trapdoor claw-free function family
description: A family of two-to-one functions for which finding a colliding pair (a claw) is computationally hard, while a secret trapdoor allows inversion, instantiated from the learning-with-errors assumption.
source_article: Verifying quantum computations at scale: a cryptographic leash on quantum devices, Thomas Vidick, 2020

name: Mahadev's classical verification theorem
description: Assuming the quantum hardness of learning with errors, there is an interactive protocol by which a classical verifier can verify the output of an arbitrary polynomial-time quantum computation performed by a single quantum prover.
source_article: Verifying quantum computations at scale: a cryptographic leash on quantum devices, Thomas Vidick, 2020

name: Cryptographic measurement protocol (qubit commitment)
description: A cryptographic primitive that forces a quantum prover to commit to a qubit and later reveal a measurement in a basis chosen by the verifier, so the prover cannot cheat across bases, built from trapdoor claw-free functions.
source_article: Verifying quantum computations at scale: a cryptographic leash on quantum devices, Thomas Vidick, 2020
